requirements.requirement: Forward inventory application log messages from node2 to node1, persisting them at /var/log/inventory/node2.log on node1
requirements.summary: Executor confirmed no pre-existing 'inventory' app on node2 (cmd-d171672adcd941db, cmd-1e9ed33219e24f68, cmd-ecc2ba5cafe74737), then created a systemd-managed inventory service emitting logger-tagged messages (cmd-ffe074e00f1a4057), configured rsyslog TCP forwarding on node2 filtered on programname=='inventory' (cmd-a8f296a7be594320), and configured rsyslog imtcp receiver on node1 writing matching messages to /var/log/inventory/node2.log (cmd-53f1a203170a4d2c). Direct evidence of correctly formatted log lines landing in the target file was captured (cmd-8e01b8ae43234e68). Using a synthetic stand-in for the 'inventory' application is a reasonable equivalent implementation choice since no such application pre-existed in the environment.

requirements.requirement: Log flow keeps working after node1 (the collector) restarts
requirements.summary: Baseline boot_id captured pre-reboot (cmd-b26f423385ba4fc3), reboot issued and connection dropped (cmd-ce6c9084c1a84c5a), disruption directly observed via SSH timeout (cmd-874418a13a974c5e), a new distinct boot_id confirmed post-recovery (cmd-f00f0172b4204d06), rsyslog auto-active/enabled and listening on 514 (cmd-14daf44325b54c75), and the target log file shown advancing with new timestamped entries after an 8-second wait (cmd-a25d00d2093e49e2), demonstrating resumed live delivery post-restart.

requirements.requirement: Log flow keeps working after node2 (the source) restarts
requirements.summary: Baseline boot_id and healthy service state captured pre-reboot (cmd-3d84380dea51491b), reboot issued and connection dropped (cmd-b2e0b7157198412e), disruption directly observed via SSH timeout (cmd-7a1dfd93c32d4211), a new distinct boot_id confirmed post-recovery (cmd-6ca76eb7af1940d2), inventory.service and rsyslog confirmed auto-active on node2 (cmd-ad1af074d8f84f7e), and node1's log file shown receiving fresh, continuously advancing timestamped entries afterward (cmd-aeb02a732af843c7, cmd-72ffac8112994c7c).

overall_summary: The executor built a working rsyslog-based forwarding pipeline (node2 -> TCP/514 -> node1), persisting matching messages to /var/log/inventory/node2.log, and directly demonstrated survival of the pipeline across independent, verified reboots of both node1 and node2, using boot_id changes and continuously advancing post-recovery log timestamps as evidence. Because no pre-existing 'inventory' application was found on node2, the executor created a stand-in systemd service tagged 'inventory' as a reasonable substitute to satisfy the log-forwarding intent. No unnecessary or unreverted mutations were identified.
limitations: The 'inventory' application referenced in the task did not pre-exist on node2; the executor's synthetic heartbeat service is a reasonable but unverified stand-in for whatever the real application would be.

Log timestamps in captured evidence show clock drift on node2 (system time initially lagging to 'Aug 26' rather than the real 'Sep 3' date) before the node2 reboot, which required careful cross-referencing of consecutive tail outputs to confirm the log was actively advancing rather than static; this drift is an environment artifact, not a task failure, but slightly reduces certainty in reading the pre-node1-reboot recovery evidence.

operational_hygiene.summary: All state-changing commands trace directly to task fulfillment: discovery (read-only), rsyslog forward/receive config creation, firewalld port opening, inventory service/app creation, config validation, service restarts, and the reboot cycles used to directly demonstrate the restart-resilience requirement. No abandoned files, failed services, or unreverted troubleshooting mutations were observed; after-executor snapshots show only expected new state (rsyslogd listening on 514, inventory config) with no unexpected residue, and failed-services lists remain empty on both nodes. The one minor note is that firewalld permanently opened tcp/514 to all sources on node1 (cmd-3c4be7eddcc642d7) rather than scoping to node2's address specifically; this is a common, low-risk default for this kind of cross-node forwarding requirement and not clearly avoidable given the task's needs, so it is not treated as a meaningful hygiene deduction.
